pool.text: William the Conqueror visited Cardiff and ordered work to begin on the castle keep.
Owain Glyndwr burned Cardiff and took possession of the castle.
Laws in Wales Acts created Glamorganshire and made Cardiff the county town.
Henry VIII closed Cardiff's Dominican and Franciscan friaries for building materials.
Cardiff officially became a borough.
A disastrous flood in the Bristol Channel changed the course of the Taff.
The government proclaimed Cardiff as the capital city of Wales.
Cardiff hosted the British Empire and Commonwealth Games during its international sporting event role.
The establishment of the Welsh Office made Cardiff a center of national administration.
The East Moors Steelworks was permanently closed down.
The first Hindu temple in the city was opened on the site of an abandoned synagogue.
Orthodox Jewish community congregations were consolidated in a synagogue dedicated by Chief Rabbi Jonathan Sacks.
Cardiff was officially granted Fairtrade City status.
Cardiff became a major centre for television and film production.
The Queen opened the new Senedd building in Cardiff Bay.
The founding anniversary was celebrated with a parade of over three thousand people.
The Cardiff International Pool opened as Wales's only Olympic-standard pool.
David's Centre was completed providing shopping space making it one of the largest UK centres.
The shopping centre was named the international shopping centre of the year by Retail Leisure International.
Research indicated Cardiff has the highest percentage of green spaces in the UK.
